message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that takes roughly **six weeks** (about 42 days) when performed under normal conditions. Here’s why: | Factor | Details | |--------|---------| | **Height** | 324 m (1,063 ft) | | **Surface area** | Roughly 10,000 m² (≈107,000 ft²) – this includes all the exposed metal panels, arches, and structural elements. | | **Work schedule** | The tower is usually worked on during the night to avoid disrupting visitors. Workers operate in shifts, often 12‑hour nights. | | **Phases** | 1️⃣ **Cleaning & preparation** – removing old paint, rust, and debris.
2️⃣ **Priming** – applying a protective primer coat.
3️⃣ **Topcoat** – applying the final color layers. | | **Safety & logistics** | Extensive scaffolding, rope access, and safety harnesses are used. Paint is applied in small sections to maintain stability and safety. | | **Frequency** | The tower is repainted every 7–8 years; each repaint cycle lasts about 6 weeks. | So if you’re planning a hypothetical repaint, expect a continuous, intensive effort lasting about six weeks, with workers operating mostly at night and covering the entire 10,000 m² surface area in stages.
